A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAPO estimation work despite the GT-to-IGC-Net renaming. Matching equations, algorithms, and benchmark results establish continuity. Text, mathematical content, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original tumor-growth simulations, semi-synthetic MIMIC-III experiments, ablations, and pseudo-outcome sensitivity results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds factual MIMIC-III prediction, robustness tests, and uncertainty analyses in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The core architecture, detached pseudo-outcome generation, regression loss, and training algorithm remain unchanged; v2 already includes the LSTM alternative. v3 adds an optional predictive-uncertainty extension using MC dropout and kernel smoothing in Appendix F.3.

E1.justification: v3 extends the retained tumor and semi-synthetic MIMIC-III coverage to factual ICU outcome prediction using actual treatments and outcomes. It also introduces a scenario with a deliberately unobserved patient confounder, changing the information available to the estimators.

E2.justification: v3 adds Xiong et al.'s G-transformer to both retained main benchmark comparisons, alongside the unchanged CRN, TE-CDE, CT, RMSNs, and G-Net baselines. This new comparator is distinct from v2's proposed G-transformer, which becomes IGC-Net.

E3.justification: New protocols include factual prediction across sample sizes and horizons, treatment-logit scaling with rho from 0.5 to 1.5, and hidden-confounder perturbations with omega from 0 to 0.020. Original benchmark settings and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged. The tumor horizon sweep in v2 Figure 5 is omitted.

E4.justification: v3 adds explicit overlap and hidden-confounding robustness tests and a coefficient-of-variation stability analysis. Existing LSTM/biased-transformer ablations and pseudo-outcome corruption tests are retained. The tumor prediction-horizon analysis in v2 Figure 5 is removed.

E5.justification: Five-run benchmark averages and their ± values remain, although v3 drops the captions explicitly identifying standard deviations over seeds. Appendix F adds MC-dropout predictive uncertainty with kernel smoothing and coefficient-of-variation reporting. There is no reported increase in benchmark run counts.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results in v2 Tables 2–3 remain unchanged in v3 Tables 3–4. v3 adds G-transformer scores, factual prediction and robustness tables, and uncertainty/stability results, while removing v2 Figure 5. For example, the new factual experiment reports RMSE 9.42 for IGC-Net versus 9.32 for CT at N=1000 and tau=2.

T1.justification: The identification assumptions and all three propositions and proofs are retained; Proposition 3 already appears in v2 Appendix C. v3 corrects outcome/history indices in the recursive expectations and adds supporting mathematical treatments of Q-learning connections and computational complexity in Appendices A and I.1.

C1.justification: The central claim of neural regression-based iterative G-computation for CAPOs remains. v3 removes the front matter's categorical low-estimation-variance promise and emphasizes avoiding inverse propensity weighting and full-distribution estimation. It presents the contribution more generally as an end-to-end neural learning algorithm.

C2.justification: New Appendix B substantially discusses clinical applicability and the plausibility of identification assumptions. v3 explicitly limits factual MIMIC-III results to a sanity check rather than causal validation and interprets performance under overlap and hidden-confounding perturbations. The explanation accompanying v2's declining-error tumor horizon results disappears with that analysis.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new logit-scaling and hidden-confounder constructions and changes the advertised code location from G_transformer to IGC_net. Existing architecture details, tuning grids, optimizer, hardware, and runtime figures are retained. Specific tuning information for the added G-transformer baseline and detailed uncertainty-sampling settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through comparisons with G-transformer, longitudinal meta-learners, survival pseudo-observations, and Q-learning/reinforcement learning. Appendix A explicitly locates novelty in jointly implementing the multi-step recursion within a neural architecture rather than introducing regression adjustment as an identification strategy.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, terminology changes throughout, and Section 4.4 consolidates comparisons. Data-generating descriptions move to an appendix, the algorithm moves into the main text, and proofs and examples are reorganized. These changes extend beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 adds a recursion diagram, new result tables, and an uncertainty plot, and redisplays existing ablations as a main-text bar chart. It redesigns and promotes the G-Net comparison table, relocates the confounding diagram, removes the trajectory illustration and tumor-horizon plot, and substantially changes figure sizing and text wrapping.

improvement.justification: The added relevant comparator, hidden-confounding tests, and clearer distinction between factual prediction and causal validation make the evidence more informative. However, new experiments have limited implementation detail, uncertainty receives no calibration evaluation, and some interpretations overreach: Table 6 reports CT outperforming IGC-Net at rho=0.6 despite claiming universal superiority. Together with the removed tumor-horizon analysis, these limitations temper the benefits to a modest overall improvement.
